title: Streaming Speech-to-Speech — Moshi, Hibiki, and Full-Duplex Dialogue
service: Duplex: a toy full-duplex speech-to-speech backend with Mimi-style codes, a Moshi-style step loop, a session log, an inner-monologue aligner, a two-way session monitor and the acoustic delay layout

parts.lesson_anchor: The Moshi architecture (12.5 Hz x 8 codebooks, depth transformer); Build It, Step 3: user_mimi[0..t], moshi_mimi[0..t-1], moshi_text[0..t-1], text before audio; code/main.py's main loop and its append order
planted_bugs: SAMPLES_PER_FRAME = SAMPLE_RATE / FRAME_RATE is the float 1920.0; the TypeError surfaces in split_frames' range(), not at the constant
DuplexSession.hear iterates encode()'s codebook-major codes as if they were frames; the ValueError surfaces one call down, in DuplexStepper.step
step predicts first and appends all three histories at the end, so frame t is predicted before user frame t is heard, and user frame s is paired with the model's output of step s instead of s - 1
_context replays the whole session every step, O(T^2): no KV cache
parts.timing_assert: 1500 steps (2 minutes of dialogue) under 0.1 s; the replaying version takes about 1.6-2.0 s, the incremental one about 6-10 ms
parts.overfix_guard: encode keeps Mimi's codebook-major layout and 1920 samples per frame (rules out transposing in the codec and FRAME_RATE = 12); after 100 probe steps the context still holds frame 0 (rules out replaying only a recent window to get fast); the probe records the user frame and model audio folded in last (rules out padding the context with one start frame so that the count comes out right, and code 0 in place of AUDIO_START)
parts.deviation: The frame-index off-by-one is the step loop hearing the user one frame late (the lesson's user_mimi[0..t]), caught by a recording probe model. The semantic/acoustic ordering defect is a codebook-major versus frame-major layout mix-up, the real-world form of that mistake; the depth transformer's codebook order is checked by the probe as a guard. Converting frames to milliseconds moved to Part 5 (ready_ms, the 160 ms floor) and seconds to frames to Part 3, where each is part of the core logic.

parts.lesson_anchor: All three streams (user audio, Moshi audio, Moshi text) run in parallel, frame by frame; the session log is what training and replay read back
parts.exactness: both sides of a frame round-trip as lists of ints, including code 0, code 1023 and PAD = 0, across close and reopen, with the two sides written separately and in any order

parts.deviation: The uplink task and the generation loop log the two sides of a frame separately, so the store has to merge halves and expose only complete frames; this is where full-duplex logging differs from logging a pipeline.

parts.lesson_anchor: Why inner-monologue text helps: the text stream is the transcript of what Moshi says, aligned to its 80 ms audio frames; transcripts for free

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Steps 1-2: both directions run simultaneously over one session; Moshi hears the user while speaking, can be interrupted, keeps emitting frames while the user talks
parts.wire_format: NDJSON, one object per frame, decided by the test's join/splitlines/json.loads

parts.deviation: The two async streams are a live session's uplink and downlink, merged by frame number into one timeline with overlap and barge-in flags. The model's silent frames are part of the input contract (a packet every 80 ms, voiced false while listening), so silence must not be confused with a lost packet. Backpressure, cancellation and turn-taking state machines belong to lessons 11 and 14 and are left out.

parts.lesson_anchor: Theoretical latency 160 ms = 80 ms Mimi frame + 80 ms acoustic delay; semantic codebook 0 then acoustic codebooks 1-7
